articles.author: Samarth Gambhir
articles.description:
In modern backend development, microservices are everywhere, and for good reason.
Instead of building a giant monolithic application, we break the system into smaller, focused services, each responsible for doing one thing well. This is the essence of microservice architecture:
One service = One responsibility
Each service = Independently deployable
Services talk to each other = System communication
For example, in an e-commerce platform:
| Service            | Responsibility                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| OrderService       | Accepts and creates new orders  |
| SMSService         | Sends SMS notifications         |
| EmailService       | Sends order confirmation emails |
| InventoryService   | Updates product stock           |


Each service:…
articles.title: From Microservices to Fan-Out: Evolving Cross-Service Communication in Modern Systems

articles.author: Mariano Álvarez 🇨🇷
articles.description:
In my previous post, I walked through how to build a basic AI agent using ADK. It’s exciting to get an agent running and see it respond to prompts — but once the session ends, that context is gone. It has no memory of anything that happened before.
This is fine for demos, but if you’re aiming to build something real then you’ll quickly hit a wall.
Fortunately, ADK gives us tools to fix that.
Let’s say you build a ticket finder agent that helps someone search for flights. During the conversation, the user mentions that they prefer Delta and want to fly out of San Francisco.
Without session management, the agent forgets all of that context between interactions. So even if the user follows up with, “What about something cheaper?” the agent has no clue what they’re referring to.
That’s where S…
articles.title: Adding Sessions and Memory to Your AI Agent with Agent Development Kit (ADK)
